text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.67% today, extending a two-week gain of 5.13%. The sharp move follows a jump of $4 in the last two trading days, driven by a significant widening between U.S. and global crude prices. U.S. oil is trading at $103.37 per barrel while world oil sits at $123.10—a $19.73 gap that reflects tightness in American supply and strong demand for U.S. production. As a major oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when this spread widens, since it sells into both markets.

The broader context is a shift in energy geopolitics: diplomatic efforts between the U.S. and Iran are progressing through Qatari mediation and public statements from Trump officials about ending tensions "peacefully," which initially drove crude lower on Monday. However, the price differential has since reversed, suggesting markets are pricing in either skepticism about the talks holding or confidence that U.S. production constraints will persist regardless of geopolitical resolution—both scenarios favor domestic producers like ConocoPhillips.
